newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar slips on news GDP to be revised.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar slips on news GDP to be revised.

text.p: The Singapore dollar weakened slightly on Wednesday following news that the city-state's 1996 growth forecast would be revised next month.
Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong was quoted by state television as saying Singapore would announce a new 1996 growth forecast in mid-November.
Yeo was also quoted as saying Singapore's fourth quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) would be fairly weak, but the extent would only be known in the next two weeks.
Forex dealers said the U.S. dollar looked slightly better bid against the Singapore dollar after the news, but this was also because the U.S. unit rose against the majors in the afternoon.
The Singapore dollar was quoted at 1.4150/60 to the U.S. dollar at 0830 GMT, after the close of Asian trading, against its opening of 1.4137/1.4147.
"The Sing's weakened from 1.4135/38 levels to 1.4150/53. The dollar looks quite bid and has found a base (against the majors) as well," said a European bank dealer.
But he said the U.S. dollar would need to close above a key technical level of S$1.4160/65 during Asian trade before it could head higher.

Dealers said the market had expected a revision to the official growth forecast after Singapore reported a surprise 6.2 percent fall in non-oil domestic exports for September and economists revised their GDP projections downwards.

Singapore's most recent official forecast was that the economy would grow by seven to eight percent in 1996, but the island has been hit by a global slump in demand for electronic products, on which it is heavily dependant in recent months.
